title: Amazon DynamoDB Extractor — Root Configuration (parameters)
description: Reads documents from Amazon DynamoDB tables and stores them as Storage tables. One set of AWS credentials in `db` is shared by every entry in `exports`; each export reads one table, either by scanning it or by querying it with a key condition, and maps the resulting documents onto CSV columns. This component is not row-based — all exports live in this root configuration.

db.title: DynamoDB Connection
db.description: AWS credentials and endpoint shared by all exports

options.tooltip: The regional DynamoDB service endpoint, in the form `https://dynamodb.REGION.amazonaws.com`. It has to point at the same region as the Region field below.

regionName.title: Region
regionName.description: AWS region the table lives in

options.tooltip: AWS region code, e.g. `eu-central-1` or `us-east-1`. It is shown next to the table in the AWS DynamoDB console.

accessKeyId.title: Access Key ID
accessKeyId.description: Access key ID of the AWS user reading the table

options.tooltip: Create an access key for an IAM user that is allowed to read the table, in the AWS console under IAM → Users → Security credentials → Create access key.

#secretAccessKey.title: Secret Access Key
#secretAccessKey.description: Secret access key belonging to the access key ID

options.tooltip: AWS shows this value only once, at the moment the access key is created. If it was not saved then, create a new access key. The value is stored encrypted.

exports.title: Exports
exports.description: One entry per exported table; at least one has to be enabled

id.title: Export ID
id.description: Unique whole number identifying this export

options.tooltip: Any whole number that is unique within this configuration. It is never sent to DynamoDB — it only distinguishes exports from one another.

name.title: Export Name
name.description: Unique name the output table is named after

options.tooltip: Slugified and used as the output table name, so it has to be unique across exports. A duplicate name fails the job with `Please remove duplicate export names`.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether this export runs; omitting it means enabled

options.tooltip: A disabled export is skipped without failing the job. If every export is disabled the job fails with `Please enable at least one export`.

mode.title: Read Mode
mode.description: How documents are read; omitting it means Scan

options.tooltip: **Scan** walks the whole table or index and can be narrowed with a date filter. **Query** fetches only the documents matching a key condition, which is far cheaper on large tables but needs a partition key value. Scan and Query accept different fields — a field belonging to the other mode makes the job fail.
Exact, case-sensitive table name as listed in the AWS DynamoDB console.

index.title: Index (Scan Mode)
index.description: Secondary index to scan instead of the table itself

options.tooltip: Used only in Scan mode. In Query mode this field is ignored — use Secondary Index instead.

indexName.title: Secondary Index
indexName.description: Secondary index to query instead of the table's own key

options.tooltip: Leave empty to query the table's own primary key. Query mode only — setting it on a Scan export fails the job.

keyConditionExpression.title: Key Condition Expression
keyConditionExpression.description: Condition selecting the documents to fetch

options.tooltip:
Required in Query mode. Compares key attributes against placeholders defined in Expression Attribute Values:

```
title = :a
$yr = :a AND title = :b
```

Use a `$`-prefixed token for any attribute name that needs escaping and declare it in Expression Attribute Names.

expressionAttributeNames.title: Expression Attribute Names
expressionAttributeNames.description: Substitution tokens for attribute names used in the key condition

options.tooltip:
Needed when an attribute name collides with a DynamoDB reserved word, such as `year`. DynamoDB tokens normally start with `#`, but Keboola encrypts every `#`-prefixed key, so write `$` instead — the component rewrites it to `#` before calling AWS:

```json
{ "$yr": "year" }
```

Query mode only.

expressionAttributeValues.title: Expression Attribute Values
expressionAttributeValues.description: Values substituted into the key condition placeholders

options.tooltip:
Every placeholder used in the key condition has to be defined here, keyed by its `:` name:

```json
{ ":a": "2013" }
```

Query mode only.

dateFilter.title: Date Filter (Scan Mode)
dateFilter.description: Keeps only documents at or after a date computed at run time

options.tooltip: Scan mode only — setting it on a Query export fails the job. All three fields have to be filled in together. The filter applied is `field >= date(format, strtotime(value))`, so the table needs a field holding a comparable date string.
Name of a field present on every document, holding a date in the format below.

format.title: Date Format
format.description: PHP date format the stored values use

options.tooltip: A PHP `date()` format string matching how the field is stored, for example `Y-m-d`, `Y-m-d H:i:s` or `Y` for a bare year.

value.title: From
value.description: Start of the range, relative or absolute

options.tooltip: Parsed with PHP `strtotime()`, so both relative values (`-2 days`, `today`, `-10 hours`) and absolute ones (`2018-01-01`) work. A value `strtotime()` cannot parse fails the job.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Maximum number of documents to export

options.tooltip: Omit to export every matching document. Documents are always fetched in batches of up to 1000; the limit only caps the total.

incremental.title: Load Type
incremental.description: How the output table is written to Storage

options.tooltip: Incremental load appends rows and updates existing ones matched by the primary key. Full load replaces the table contents on every run.

primaryKey.title: Primary Key
primaryKey.description: Output columns forming the table's primary key

options.tooltip: Every name listed here has to be one of the destination column names produced by the mapping, otherwise the job fails with `Primary keys do not match columns`. Required in practice for an incremental load to deduplicate.

mapping.title: Mapping
mapping.description: Maps document fields onto output columns
